claims.text: The local Nintendo 64 W Double Get Campaign source slice models two currently source-pinned rows: Cool Porygon and Hungry Snorlax.
The selected Pokumon lines place the campaign between December 10, 1997 and January 31, 1998.
The selected Pokumon lines describe the cards as given to customers at participating stores who purchased a Nintendo 64, together with the Singing Pokemon Encyclopedia music CD.
The selected Pokumon lines describe the cards as contained in a booklet sealed with the music CD, with two Food counters stored behind Hungry Snorlax for use with its attacks.
The selected Pokumon lines say Cool Porygon and Hungry Snorlax were later reprinted in Pokemon Song Best Collection CD and describe those reprints as identical to the Nintendo 64 campaign versions.
The local source-pinned rows credit Cool Porygon to Hiromichi Sugiyama and Hungry Snorlax to Sumiyoshi Kizuki.
The campaign shows Pokemon as a bundled media apparatus: a Nintendo 64 hardware purchase, music CD, booklet, two promo cards, and physical Food counters all sharing one collector object.

Agents should separate N64 W Double Get campaign identity from later Song Best Collection packaging, English Wizards Black Star Cool Porygon, generic CD promos, generic Snorlax/Porygon listings, and seller claims of sealed CD/booklet/Food-counter completeness.

chase_cards.name: Cool Porygon
chase_cards.why: It is a Porygon card tied directly to Nintendo hardware retail memory, then later pulled into Song Best and English promo memory. The hard part is keeping the route legible instead of collapsing every Cool Porygon into one bucket.

chase_cards.name: Hungry Snorlax
chase_cards.why: It is the more physical of the two: the booklet apparently stored Food counters behind the card, so the card's play idea spills into a little paper-object kit.

key_artists.name: Hiromichi Sugiyama
key_artists.why: Cool Porygon's credit matters because Porygon is already a character about artificial construction; here it becomes a hardware-purchase promo whose afterlife crosses into CD and English promo channels.

key_artists.name: Sumiyoshi Kizuki
key_artists.why: Hungry Snorlax's credit sits on the campaign's most tactile object: a Snorlax card with Food counters stored behind it, where illustration, rule text, and packaging all ask to be kept together.

narrative.human_title: Nintendo 64 W Double Get: Pokemon becomes a bundled machine
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of those little promo lanes where the whole apparatus peeks through. A child did not only get a card; the story runs through a Nintendo 64 purchase, a music CD, a sealed booklet, two promo cards, and Hungry Snorlax's Food counters. Cool Porygon makes the hardware-memory obvious, Hungry Snorlax makes it tactile, and the later Song Best reuse turns the pair into a route-identification puzzle. The cards are charming, but the real collector pulse is the bundle: Pokemon learning how to move through stores, machines, songs, paper, and play pieces at once.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, seller story, slab label, or agent memory says Nintendo 64 W Double Get Campaign, N64 promo, Cool Porygon, Hungry Snorlax, Kakkoii Porygon, Kuishinbo Kabigon, Singing Pokemon Encyclopedia, Pokemon Song Best Collection, CD promo, Food counters, sealed booklet, Wizards Black Star Cool Porygon, or Space World 1997.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Keep the two-card N64 purchase-campaign route legible while separating it from Song Best, English Cool Porygon, and generic CD-promo claims.
steps: Confirm the campaign route is Nintendo 64 W Double Get Campaign, not merely a generic CD promo or English Wizards Black Star Cool Porygon listing.
Confirm the modeled pair is Cool Porygon and Hungry Snorlax, local source rows 028 and 029.
Check the claimed date/context against the December 10, 1997-January 31, 1998 purchase-campaign window.
If the seller mentions the Singing Pokemon Encyclopedia CD, sealed booklet, or Food counters, record those as provenance objects to inspect, not automatic proof that the card is campaign-distributed.
Separate the N64 campaign source slice from the later Pokemon Song Best Collection CD release, even when the card versions are described as identical.
Separate Japanese Cool Porygon / Hungry Snorlax from English Wizards Black Star Cool Porygon and from ordinary Porygon or Snorlax prints.
Preserve Hiromichi Sugiyama and Sumiyoshi Kizuki credits as illustrator context, but do not treat artist credit as route proof.

Before any trade gate or spendability decision, require seller-controlled front/back images, close-ups of title, copyright/layout, artwork, surface/corners, and evidence for any claimed CD/booklet/Food-counter/sealed-object completeness.

narrative.human_title: Cool Porygon: a digital Pokemon tied to a console purchase
narrative.why_it_matters: Cool Porygon is almost too perfect as an artifact. Porygon is a made thing inside the fiction, and this card is attached to a made thing in the world: the Nintendo 64. Its later Song Best and English lives are part of the charm, but also the danger. A good agent should enjoy the route and refuse to blur it.

narrative.human_title: Hungry Snorlax: the promo with pieces behind it
narrative.why_it_matters: Hungry Snorlax is lovable because the card points past itself. The selected campaign lines keep returning to the booklet and the Food counters tucked behind the card, as if Snorlax dragged a little lunchbox of game pieces into the promo object. That is the kind of detail a collector remembers.
